newsitem.title: MEXICO: Femsa Q3 sales volumes encourage analysts.
newsitem.headline: Femsa Q3 sales volumes encourage analysts.

text.p: Mexico's Fomento Economico Mexicano S.A. (Femsa) posted higher-than-expected sales volumes in the third quarter this year, a pleasant surprise that shows Mexican beer consumption may be pulling out of the doldrums, analysts said on Tuesday.
Femsa is Mexico's second-largest beer-maker to Grupo Modelo and a bottler of soft drinks. Femsa also owns the Coke Femsa distributor of Coca-Cola in Mexico and Argentina.

Femsa reported this week a nine-months net of 1.189 billion pesos versus 736.9 million during the same period of last year. Much of the gain, however, was due to non-cash financial gains -- sales revenues were largely flat.
Analysts were taking a closer look at the beer sales volumes because soft drinks already had shown signs of recovery.
Domestic sales volumes rose 11.5 percent in the quarter to 4.94 million hectoliters, this after some analysts were predicting that a 10 percent increase would be a stretch.
Still, volumes are lagging behind the company's prediction of a 20 percent increase at the start of the year, analysts said.

"I was really pleased to see the domestic sales volumes much better than expected," said Laura Ehrlich, an analyst with Paribas in New York. "However, it was offset by two factors: a reduction in price in real terms and that the exports were very disappointing."
Exports fell 9.5 percent to 257,000 hectoliters, largely because of disappointing sales in South America and Europe. Prices have held steady since an increase in the second quarter.
The good news is that U.S. sales grew by 27 percent in the quarter quarter, Ehrlich said.
But Femsa also faces "serious problems" in trying to keep up with Modelo, said Thomas Mobille, an analyst with Robert Fleming in Brazil.

"Femsa has some distribution problems," Mobille said. "They were using their own distribution trying to crack new markets, but that's awfully expensive when you don't have the market share. So they've contracted out. It's not the kind of thing a company can feel really good about when they're saying they can't compete the same way their main competition does."

Also, operating margin fell to 8.8 percent in the third quarter from 11 percent in the second quarter, but that can be attributed to the price increase in the second quarter. Analysts said they don't expect another price increase this year.
Greg Rianhard, an analyst with D.A. Campbell in Los Angeles, said the higher sales volumes were fueled by Femsa's Sol brand, which competes with Modelo's Corona as a premium beer.

"What interests be about Femsa is Sol," Rianhard said. "They (the company) say they are not spending a large amount of their advertising budget on Sol. They say it sells itself. If that's true it's very positive."
